analysis:
Scope: one documentation file, docs/architecture/inference.md, head lines 1-801. No code was supplied. The visible changes are the date bump at line 3 and the GLM weight-hash paragraph at head lines 684-691. The changed GLM video text (head 818-821, 837, 884-903) and lines 1740-1759 fall outside these units, so that text was not examined here.

Lines 684-691 say the published GLM weight hash is now the manifest aggregate (GLM5NextManagedLoad.verifiedArtifactSHA256, ProviderLoop.verifiedGLM5NextWeightHash). Separate pre- and post-load WeightHasher passes are dropped. The next coordinator-mode start may register the cached hash without reading weights, provided each file's device, inode, size, mtime and ctime are unchanged (VerifiedWeightHashStore). The doc says the load verifies again before serving.

Relevant threats are T-012, T-027, T-034, A-004 and A-011. ADV-001 has root access and can manipulate file metadata, including ctime by changing the clock. If a load re-verified every file before serving, a stat-based cache would only affect the registration-time claim. A-004 already treats the weight hash as provider-reported rather than an attestation. On that basis, documentation evidence alone does not show a regression.

Open questions for integration:
- Verify in VerifiedWeightHashStore and ProviderLoop that the registration-time cached hash cannot be published for weights that were later swapped.
- Verify that the before-serving re-verification hashes content and refuses on mismatch.
- Check whether T-012/T-027 should record the stat-identity shortcut.

The remaining text (Nemotron Super slot, prefix bank scoped by authenticated cache scope, GLM admission) is unchanged surrounding context. One point is consistent with T-041: coordinator text prefix reuse is partitioned by authenticated scope, image prefix reuse is scope- and feature-bound, and nothing is reused without a scope (lines 232-238, 527-530). No new findings.
